title: Multiclass Classification Strategies knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the central idea of “Multiclass Classification Strategies”?
options: The method proves that every prediction will be correct on all future datasets.
The method removes the need to inspect data quality or define an evaluation strategy.
The method always performs better than a simple baseline, regardless of the task.
Classification assigns class labels or estimates class probabilities. The threshold, class balance, calibration, and error costs affect which evaluation metric is useful.
questions.answer_key: Classification assigns class labels or estimates class probabilities. The threshold, class balance, calibration, and error costs affect which evaluation metric is useful.
questions.explanation: The lesson frames the topic this way: Classification assigns class labels or estimates class probabilities. The threshold, class balance, calibration, and error costs affect which evaluation metric is useful. The other options make unsupported guarantees.

questions.prompt: What is a sound first step when applying “Multiclass Classification Strategies” to a new task?
options: Remove records that produce unexpected outcomes without investigating them.
Assume the default parameters are best for every dataset.
Name the inputs, assumptions, and output for One-versus-rest classification; then test it on representative data.
Tune against the final test set until the preferred metric increases.
questions.answer_key: Name the inputs, assumptions, and output for One-versus-rest classification; then test it on representative data.
questions.explanation: Define the input, output, assumptions, and evidence needed. For One-versus-rest classification, a small representative check is more useful than blind tuning.

questions.prompt: What conclusion is appropriately cautious after trying “Multiclass Classification Strategies”?
options: An internal estimator score replaces domain review and operational monitoring.
A successful small example is useful evidence about that example, but generalization, risks, and limitations still need separate checks.
A single successful run proves fairness, robustness, and production readiness.
A higher training score alone proves generalization to unseen data.
questions.answer_key: A successful small example is useful evidence about that example, but generalization, risks, and limitations still need separate checks.
questions.explanation: A demonstration only supports conclusions within its scope. Evaluate representative unseen cases and report limitations before production use.
